_comment: ONE CORPUS, TWO READERS (M5 stage A, deliverable 1).
harness/src/trace.cpp's TraceReader::next and tools/tracefile.py's
read_capture implement the same record-form contract in two languages.
'The two must agree on what they accept and what they reject' is a claim,
and this file is what makes it a test: test_trace_records.cpp replays it
through the C++ reader and tracefile.selfcheck() replays it through the
Python one, and each asserts the verdict recorded here.
SCOPE, stated so the corpus is not read as more than it is: these cases
cover the `kind` DISCRIMINATOR's contract -- the thing this stage added.
They do not cover every structural rule the C++ reader enforces (the venue
metadata contract, rx_ns monotonicity, the `type` rule), because the Python
reader deliberately does not enforce those: read_meta's `validate` is
opt-in, for the reason its own docstring gives. Adding a rule to either
reader means adding its case here, and that is the point of the file.
Every case is a RECORD LINE. The header is supplied by whichever test reads
this, because the two readers want different things from it and the header
is not what is under test. `accept` is the verdict; `form` is the record
form a reader must report when it accepts; `why` is for the human reading a
failure.
ADD CASES. Never quietly relax one: a case that starts failing is either a
reader that changed what a committed file means, or a contract that moved
on purpose -- and the second wants a sentence in a commit message.

cases.name: plain frame, no kind key
cases.why: the shape every record in every trace committed before 2026-08-24 has; an absent kind is what makes the key additive

cases.name: a frame this side sent
cases.why: dir and kind are independent keys in the same wrapper slot; a tx record is still a frame

cases.name: rest, fully formed
cases.why: a transcript plus a question: the body means nothing without the url and limit that produced it

cases.name: control ping, fully formed
cases.why: the record that is not a frame at all: a ping payload is arbitrary bytes, so frame is null

cases.name: control close, no reply recorded
cases.why: pong_ns is optional and its ABSENCE is meaningful -- a close carries no reply, and neither does a ping nobody answered

cases.name: unknown kind
cases.why: refused BY NAME rather than read as a plain frame: an unknown kind is a capture written by a newer tool, and filing it as a venue frame puts a record nobody understands in a counter that claims to describe the wire

cases.name: control with a non-null frame
cases.why: a control record with something to say is a record that cannot be true

cases.name: control with no ctl object
cases.why: ctl is the only thing a control record has, the frame being null by definition

cases.name: control with no recv_ns
cases.why: recv_ns is the ARRIVAL; the record's own rx_ns is when the main loop wrote it, and three pings 20 s apart can share one

cases.name: control with no op
cases.why: the opcode is the record's kind name, and a ping and a close are opposite evidence about the same socket

cases.name: rest with no req object
cases.why: a response body whose request is unknown cannot be reconciled against anything

cases.name: rest with no limit
cases.why: a limit=100 book and a limit=1000 book are different claims about the same instrument, and limit=100 is wrong within 90 seconds on BTCUSDT

cases.name: rest with no url
cases.why: which instrument, on which host, at which API version -- none of it is recoverable from the body

cases.name: rest whose fetch failed, recorded not dropped
cases.why: ACCEPTED, and the reader learned it from the wire: capture_binance.py records a failed fetch because 'the snapshot did not arrive' is a fact about the capture window. It re-baselines nothing, and both readers name it rest:no-body rather than folding it into the fetch count

cases.name: rest whose frame is neither an object nor null
cases.why: object-or-null is the whole rule; a number is neither a book nor an absence of one

cases.name: a frame body carrying the kind marker in its text
cases.why: the venue's text must never be able to describe the record that carries it; both readers bound the kind scan to the wrapper
